idiom_name: brokered message headers: ServiceBusMessage.ApplicationProperties plus a pipeline behaviour
implementation_notes: On .NET the carrying structure is the broker SDK's message header bag - for Azure Service Bus, ServiceBusMessage.ApplicationProperties, an IDictionary<string, object> of custom metadata - so the classic history container is replaced by one reserved key plus a middleware/mutator hook that reads it on receive and rewrites it on send. Because the property bag accepts only scalar, header-friendly types (unsupported or binary values throw SerializationException at serialization time), the hop list must be serialized to a string or spread across indexed scalar keys. Rebuild the outgoing message instead of mutating a received one, and cap the list: the broker's maximum message size includes application properties.
pitfalls: ApplicationProperties throws SerializationException for unsupported types and is documented as broken for byte[]/ArraySegment<byte> - serialize the hop list as text (base64 for binary) or the send fails.
Mutating a received message's properties and forwarding it is not legal in the SDK's flow: build a new ServiceBusMessage; settlement and size checks apply per message.
Uncapped growth silently hits the broker's message-size limit including properties, so a retry loop can turn a diagnostic trail into rejected messages.
